newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids fall further.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids fall further.

text.p: Spring wheat bids tumbled once again at several country locations in line with a drop in MGE spring wheat futures, several cash grain dealers said.
"There's just nothing trading right now," a Montana dealer said. "We have no place to sell it, so what's the point of buying it?"
MGE December spring wheat futures closed at $3.78 per bushel on Tuesday after setting a fresh contract low at $3.77-1/2 per bushel. Spring wheat had peaked at $6.34 per bushel in May.
Some areas also noted sharp declines in basis levels.
In parts of Montana, basis levels fell by 15 cents per bushel as demand dried up. Brokers noted spring wheat continued to trade at a premium to soft red winter wheat.
"If (importers) are looking for the cheapest wheat, they certainly aren't going to look at spring wheat," a Minnesota dealer said.
